content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I created a circuit diagram using [product_name] with the ladder editor and added comments to the inputs, outputs, and timers to increase readability. I arranged the outputs sequentially (Q1 on the first line, Q2 on the second, Q3 on the third, etc.) and gave the diagram a name. After downloading it from my PC to the [product_name] device ([article_no]), I noticed that when I uploaded the circuit diagram back to my PC, the diagram name had changed to Circuit Diagram1, the comments were gone, and the output sequence was altered—for example, Q7 was now the first line instead of Q1. Is this expected behavior, or did I miss something when creating the diagram with [product_name]?

Comments, logical diagram layout, and similar information are stored only in the project files created by the Comfort software, not in the [product_name] device itself. When you reload the diagram from the device, the Comfort software determines its own order. To preserve your notes, comments, and structure, make sure to save and reload the program directly from the Comfort software files on your PC.
Only the code is saved in the [product_name] basic module—formatting, notes, and comments are excluded due to limited device memory. It's essential to save your [product_name] project separately.
Hi, That issue dates back some time; with newer [product_name] versions, have these features changed, or are limitations still present?
Any kind of comments are not transferred when sending the program to the [product_name] device.
Hello, Refer to this FAQ: [url] The device offers 30,000 bytes of layout memory for graphical information, such as the arrangement of function blocks and connecting lines. Regards, [user_name]

Hello. Block names are transferred to the [product_name] device, and the supported length has increased. These names will be uploaded with the program and can be helpful. Good block names are especially useful when using a device with a display, as selected parameters can be accessed through system menus. These are protected by the system password and are not available to all users. For those who access internal parameters, descriptive block names assist in selecting the correct settings. - [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: When transferring circuit diagrams between [product_name] software and [product_name] devices, users note that comments, diagram names, and output sequences are not retained—only the core logic is transferred. This leads to lost readability and organizational features, highlighting differences in how PC software and device memory process information. Some block names and graphical arrangements are partially preserved, but detailed comments and structural notes are generally not stored in the device.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that comments, diagram names, and output sequences will remain consistent when moving programs between [product_name] software and devices, keeping diagrams organized and readable.
